b: Local Linearization & Differentiability: A function \(f\) is differentiable at \(x = a\) if and only if the difference quotient \(\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}\) exists as a finite real number. Differentiability at \(x = a\) strictly implies continuity at \(x = a\), but the converse fails at sharp corners (e.g. \(|x - 2|\)), vertical tangents, or jump discontinuities.

f_ar: Definition 8.1 — IB AA SL Paper 1 Non-Calculator Techniques: Binomial, Trig & Reverse Chain Rule
b: In IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL (Paper 1, Non-Calculator): (1) The general term of \( (a + b)^n \) is \( T_{r+1} = \binom{n}{r}a^{n-r}b^r \); (2) Double-angle identities \( \sin 2\theta = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta \) and \( \cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta \) reduce quadratic trig equations; (3) By reverse chain rule, \( \int g'(x)[g(x)]^n\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{[g(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1} + C \) (\( n \neq -1 \)).
